title: the_house_that_remembered
beats: I (26F) bought a survival world seed off a stranger for $40, and I should've asked why he sold it so cheap.
The world was pre-built, some kind of custom terrain, and there was already a house standing near spawn.
The seller's note just said: 'don't go inside, just parkour on the roof, the loot is up there.'
I'm a parkour builder, so that's all I wanted anyway, I never plan to go inside houses.
The roof course was insane, tight jumps, timed pistons, genuinely some of the best parkour design I'd ever seen.
Three hours in, I clipped a jump and fell through a hole I swear wasn't there before.
I landed inside the house, in a bedroom, and the door was already open.
There was a sign on the bed that just said 'you took long enough.'
I checked the world's last-played date before this session out of habit, force of habit from reviewing old projects.
It said the world had been played 4 minutes ago, and I'd downloaded it eleven months ago and never opened it till today.
I texted the seller the screenshot, and his reply came instantly: 'delete it now, don't check the entity list.'
I checked the entity list.
One villager, tagged with a custom name: my actual real name, the one I don't use online, the one only my family knows.
I closed Minecraft, and my launcher reopened itself thirty seconds later on its own.
The world was already loading, and I was standing in that same bedroom, no loading screen, just there.
I've deleted the file four times now, and it keeps coming back in my saves folder overnight.
Last night I got brave and broke the sign by the bed to see what was under it.
Under the sign, scratched into the block itself, it said: 'ask him what happened to the last person who bought the seed.'
I never got a reply back from the seller again, his account's gone, deleted, no trace.
But someone is still typing in my Minecraft chat every night at 3AM, and it's always the same four words: 'you're almost done climbing.'
Climbing to where?
